Prompt 22 — Local-first image loading, pull-verified diagnostics, and an optional release publisher

Context
-------
Read .github/copilot-instructions.md and the newest
feedback/airgap-run-*.md files. Inspect the current artifacts.tsv,
scripts/lib.sh, scripts/00-diagnose.sh, scripts/60-load-images.sh,
scripts/62-k3s-images.sh, lab-vm.conf, versions.lock,
content/extracted/external-images.txt,
content/vendor/MANUAL-FETCH.md, and content/vendor/manual-fetch.json.

Established facts — do not re-litigate:

- The learner VM cannot reach GitHub Release URLs directly.
- Image tarballs may be downloaded elsewhere and placed on the
  learner VM by an approved transfer mechanism.
- Otherwise, images are pulled from Artifactory during provisioning.
- Organisational approval for the required images is in place. Remove
  all "unapproved image" callouts and any language that treats
  approval as a workaround or open question.
- The repository is the only normal transfer item. Local image
  archives are optional operator-provided files, not repository
  artifacts.
- Do not modify the separate Ubuntu offline-cluster workflow.

Findings from the latest diagnostic that this prompt responds to:

- The manifest probe returns HTTP 404 for images the operator can
  pull successfully on the same VM. The 404 means "not cached or not
  visible to this probe", not "unavailable". The diagnostic must
  avoid reporting these as failures.
- Container images are the only remaining artefact class that
  benefits from explicit local provision. The k3s binary and airgap
  archive already use the local-first resolver.

This task runs on the connected upstream machine only. Do not access
the learner VM or run provisioning against it.

Objective
---------
Three changes:

1. Make the diagnostic verify ambiguous manifest results with an
   actual container pull, so it reports only true failures.
2. Support one local tarball per image via the catalog so the
   operator can stage only the missing ones.
3. Add an optional online-side publisher that creates a GitHub
   Release with one tarball per required image at the pinned
   version, with retry logic for partial uploads.

Task 1 — diagnostic verifies ambiguous probes by pulling
--------------------------------------------------------
Update scripts/00-diagnose.sh. Bump SCRIPT_VERSION, add a CHANGE
comment.

For the registry image check, replace the current probe reporting
with:

1. For each image reference in
   content/extracted/external-images.txt:

   a. Attempt `podman pull <original-reference>` first. This is
      authoritative: success means the image is available; failure
      means it is not.
   b. If the pull succeeds:
      - report OK for that image, with the pull duration;
      - if the image was absent before the pull, note that the
        diagnostic warmed the local store as a side effect.
   c. If the pull fails:
      - capture the exact pull output;
      - classify the failure:
          * registry endpoint unreachable, DNS, or TLS failure →
            real FAIL with endpoint diagnostics;
          * registry reachable but image returns 404 after mirror
            resolution → real FAIL for that specific image, with
            the reference and the mirror endpoint;
          * authentication required → real FAIL with the exact
            401/403 response and a fix-hint;
          * any other failure → real FAIL with the raw output.
   d. Do not report a manifest probe result as a failure on its own.
      The manifest probe may be retained as an optional informational
      fast-path, but the pull result decides pass/fail per image.
2. The diagnostic now modifies the local Podman store by pulling
   images. This is a deliberate change from read-only behaviour:
   it is the mechanism that proves image availability and warms
   the store for provisioning.

   Update the script header comment accordingly. Add a
   `--no-pull-verification` flag that reverts to probe-only,
   read-only reporting. Default behaviour pulls. Document the
   difference in the header.

   The diagnostic no longer claims to be read-only by default.
   Update feedback/README.md to state this in the interpretation
   guidance.

3. Keep both supported registry endpoint forms:
   preferred subdomain `docker-registry.<ART_REPO_DOMAIN>` and the
   configured path form.

4. Keep reporting the k3s binary resolution, k3s airgap archive
   resolution, SELinux mode, firewalld state, DNF state, CA trust,
   ISO mount, content presence, and package availability checks
   unchanged. Skopeo absent remains SKIPPED; script 20 installs it.

Qualifying on "read-only": the previous version's contract was
read-only and exit 0. The pull-verified default changes the first
part. Preserve the exit-0 behaviour; the report classifies failures
rather than gating on them, as before.

Task 2 — one catalog row per image archive
------------------------------------------
Update learner-vm/artifacts.tsv. Replace the single catch-all
`saved-images.tar` row with one row per image, so an operator can
stage only the ones they need. Do not add GitHub-Release fields, an
IMAGE_ARCHIVE_BASE_URL, or per-image URL variables. Image archives
remain filesystem-only.

Rows to add (id | kind | required | staging path | url_variable |
sha256_lock_key | consumer | install_target):

  image-jaegertracing-all-in-one
    image-archive | no |
    images/jaegertracing-all-in-one-1.76.0.tar | - | - |
    scripts/60-load-images.sh | podman

  image-perses
    image-archive | no |
    images/persesdev-perses-v0.54.0.tar | - | - |
    scripts/60-load-images.sh | podman

  image-opensearch
    image-archive | no |
    images/opensearchproject-opensearch-3.3.1.tar | - | - |
    scripts/60-load-images.sh | podman

  image-opensearch-dashboards
    image-archive | no |
    images/opensearchproject-opensearch-dashboards-3.3.0.tar | - | - |
    scripts/60-load-images.sh | podman

  image-prometheus
    image-archive | no |
    images/prom-prometheus-v3.13.1.tar | - | - |
    scripts/60-load-images.sh | podman

  image-node-exporter
    image-archive | no |
    images/prometheus-node-exporter-v1.12.1.tar | - | - |
    scripts/60-load-images.sh | podman

  image-fluent-bit
    image-archive | no |
    images/fluent-fluent-bit-5.1.1.tar | - | - |
    scripts/60-load-images.sh | podman

  image-busybox
    image-archive | no |
    images/library-busybox-1.36.tar | - | - |
    scripts/60-load-images.sh | podman

  image-otel-collector
    image-archive | no |
    images/otel-opentelemetry-collector-contrib-0.159.0.tar | - | - |
    scripts/60-load-images.sh | podman

Use the actual references from content/extracted/external-images.txt.
If a listed image is not present there, do not add a row for it.
Filenames follow the release asset naming in Task 5 so a
downloaded asset can be placed directly at its catalogued path.

If a checksum is recorded in versions.lock against the row's
sha256_lock_key, the resolver verifies it. If not, the archive is
loaded and reported as unverified. No checksum is required.

Resolver behaviour for image-archive rows:
  1. If the file exists at its catalogued staging path:
     - verify against versions.lock if a checksum is recorded;
       mismatch is FATAL with no network call;
     - otherwise report present (unverified);
     - return the path, no network activity.
  2. If absent:
     - report SKIPPED for that image;
     - do not probe or fetch any URL;
     - the image is handled in the pull stage.
Do not load arbitrary files from the staging directory.

Task 3 — scripts/60-load-images.sh
---------------------------------
Bump SCRIPT_VERSION, add a CHANGE comment.

Verify or implement this sequence:

1. For every image-archive row in the catalog, resolve it via the
   shared helper.
2. For each resolved archive file:
   - load it with `docker load -i <path>` through the sudo wrapper
     (this loads into the rootful Podman store);
   - verify the original reference is now present via
     `docker image inspect <original-reference>`;
   - record the source as "local archive".
3. Check every required image reference against the Podman store.
4. For each image still absent, pull the original reference through
   the configured Artifactory mirror. Record the source as
   "Artifactory mirror".
5. A local archive is an optimisation and a fallback, not a
   requirement. Its absence must not fail setup if the pull
   succeeds.
6. If both paths fail for a required image: fail with the exact
   reference, the pull output, the mirror endpoint, and the
   diagnostic that shows whether the registry endpoint itself was
   reachable.
7. Write per-image results to content/extracted/built-tags.txt as
   before, extended with the source field.
8. Final exit codes: 0 all present; 1 any external pull failed; 2
   any unexpected build failure (unchanged).

Do not attempt a GitHub Release download, a public-internet fetch,
or any URL-based image acquisition. Do not load arbitrary files.

Task 4 — scripts/62-k3s-images.sh
---------------------------------
Bump SCRIPT_VERSION, add a CHANGE comment.

For each external image needed by a k3s workload:

1. If already in the k3s containerd store, skip.
2. Else if present in the Podman store (including from a local
   archive loaded by script 60): `podman save -o /tmp/<name>.tar
   <original-reference>`, then
   `k3s ctr -n k8s.io images import /tmp/<name>.tar`.
3. Else `k3s crictl pull <original-reference>` through the
   configured k3s Artifactory mirror.
4. Report the source for each image.
5. On failure, print reference, endpoint, k3s version,
   `k3s crictl images`, and journal excerpts. Do not use
   `k3s ctr images pull` for mirror access. Do not download image
   archives from URLs.

Task 5 — optional online-side release publisher
----------------------------------------------
Create scripts/dev/publish-image-release.sh. It runs on the
connected upstream machine. It is a convenience for the operator to
publish image tarballs as GitHub Release assets, so individual
missing images can be downloaded and sneakernetted to the learner
VM. The learner VM never fetches from the release.

Requirements:

Inputs:
  --tag <tag>                 release tag (required)
  --repo <owner/name>         target repository (required)
  --images-file <path>        default:
                              content/extracted/external-images.txt
  --out <dir>                 default: dist/image-release/
  --dry-run                   print actions; do not pull, upload, or
                              modify the release
  --replace-existing          replace assets that already exist
                              (default: skip them)
  --retries N                 upload retries per asset (default 3)

Behaviour:
1. Read the image list. Fail with a clear message if the file is
   empty or missing.
2. For each reference, derive a deterministic asset filename:
     <registry-stripped-path>-<tag>.tar
   where '/' becomes '-', ':' becomes '-', and known prefixes
   (library/, docker.io/, ghcr.io/, quay.io/, opensearchproject/,
   jaegertracing/, prom/, prometheus/, persesdev/, otel/) are
   preserved for readability.
   Example: docker.io/jaegertracing/all-in-one:1.76.0 →
            jaegertracing-all-in-one-1.76.0.tar
   The naming must be stable: rerunning the tool must produce the
   same filenames. List the exact filename mapping in the output.
3. Pull each image with Podman on the connected machine, then
   `podman save --format oci-archive -o <asset> <reference>`.
4. Verify every generated asset is present and has nonzero size
   before proceeding. Fail before uploading if any is missing.
5. Create or update the release:
     gh release view <tag> --repo <repo> || gh release create ...
   Do not add release notes or a tag body; use `--notes ""` and
   `--latest=false` unless the operator overrides.
6. For each asset:
   - if it already exists on the release and --replace-existing is
     not set, skip it and record it as "skipped (existing)";
   - otherwise upload with `gh release upload --clobber` and up to
     --retries attempts with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s).
   Upload individually, not as a batch: GitHub splits batch uploads
   and reports combined failures that are hard to attribute.
7. After the upload pass, list the release's assets via
     gh api repos/<repo>/releases/tags/<tag> --jq '.assets[].name'
   Compare against the expected asset set.
   Any missing asset is a candidate for the retry pass.
8. Retry pass: for each missing asset, rerun the individual upload
   with the same backoff, up to --retries attempts, then re-check.
9. Final report:
   - assets created, skipped, uploaded after retry, or still
     missing;
   - the exact reference-to-asset mapping;
   - the base URL pattern the operator can use to download each
     asset on a connected machine, for example:
       https://github.com/<repo>/releases/download/<tag>/<asset>
   - the SHA-256 of each asset, so the operator can optionally
     record it in versions.lock against the catalog row's
     sha256_lock_key and get checksum verification on the VM;
   - a plain-language "if any asset is still missing, this is a
     release-side failure, not a VM-side one — retry manually with
     gh release upload".
10. `--dry-run` performs no pulls, no saves, no uploads, and no
    release modification. It prints the asset list, filenames, and
    commands it would run.
11. Do not embed tokens in the script. Use the environment's `gh`
    authentication or a `GH_TOKEN` from the environment.
12. Do not push anything to GitHub in `--dry-run`.
13. If `gh` is not available, exit with a clear fix-hint; do not
    silently fall back to curl.

Also write a short paragraph in the script header explaining why
uploading is per-asset with retries: GitHub release uploads can
partially fail when many assets are uploaded together, so the tool
uploads individually and retries only what is missing.

Manually downloading an asset for sneakernet is the operator's
responsibility. Do not build a downloader into this script.

Task 6 — documentation
----------------------
Update content/vendor/MANUAL-FETCH.md,
content/vendor/manual-fetch.json, README-FIRST.md, and
feedback/README.md.

MANUAL-FETCH.md Section C:
- Remove the approval-notice callouts entirely.
- Document only these two image routes, in preference order:
  1. Preferred/default: pull original image references through the
     configured Artifactory mirror during provisioning.
  2. Optional local fallback: provide one tarball per image at its
     catalogued staging path
     `$MANUAL_FETCH_DIR/images/<asset_name>`. Script 60 loads any
     present archives, then pulls only the images still absent.
- Document the connected-machine asset creation:
    podman pull <original-reference>
    podman save --format oci-archive -o <asset-name>.tar \
      <original-reference>
- Document that assets are produced optionally by
  scripts/dev/publish-image-release.sh and can be downloaded
  individually for sneakernet.
- Document the VM staging:
    sudo install -d -o engineer -g engineer -m 0750 \
      /var/tmp/o11y-lab-vm-manual/images
    sudo install -o engineer -g engineer -m 0644 \
      /path/to/<asset-name>.tar \
      /var/tmp/o11y-lab-vm-manual/images/<asset-name>.tar
- State plainly that a diagnostic manifest-probe 404 is
  informational; the diagnostic's pull result is authoritative.

Regenerate manual-fetch.json from the catalog. One entry per
image-archive row. Remove all URL fields and approval notices.

README-FIRST.md runtime-recovery paragraph: reference Section C and
the staging directory in at most three sentences.

feedback/README.md interpretation guidance:
- Replace the previous wording about pull-through 404s with: "The
  diagnostic now performs real container pulls to classify image
  availability. A pull failure is the authoritative failure signal.
  A manifest-probe failure alone is informational."
- Add a note that the diagnostic is no longer read-only by default;
  it warms the local image store. The
  `--no-pull-verification` flag restores probe-only behaviour.
- Remove any "unapproved image" guidance.

Task 7 — validation
-------------------
On the connected machine only:

- bash -n and error-level ShellCheck on all changed scripts.
- pre-commit run --all-files; report the known historical EOF
  exception rather than modifying unrelated files.
- scripts/00-diagnose.sh --selftest.
- scripts/00-diagnose.sh --no-pull-verification --selftest, if the
  flag supports a synthetic mode; otherwise confirm the flag is
  parsed and the fallback behaviour is probe-only in --dry-run.
- Resolver test cases with temporary fixtures:
    a. archive present, no checksum: loaded and reported unverified;
       no network call.
    b. archive present with matching recorded checksum: loaded; no
       network call.
    c. archive present with mismatched checksum: FATAL; no network
       call; file untouched.
    d. archive absent: SKIPPED; no network call.
    e. --dry-run: no files created, no downloads attempted.
- publish-image-release.sh --dry-run: asset list printed,
  deterministic naming verified on the actual image list, no
  pulls or uploads performed.
- grep audit results:
    * no IMAGE_ARCHIVE_BASE_URL, GitHub Release publisher, or
      image-archive URL fetch in learner-VM runtime scripts;
    * no "unapproved image", "approval", or "not approved" language
      remains in active operator docs;
    * no public-internet fetch path in learner-VM scripts (public
      release URLs may appear in documentation examples only);
    * no literal `github.com` in learner-VM scripts.

Do not run provisioning against the learner VM. Do not claim the
release, image fetch, image load, or offline operation have been
tested there.

Acceptance
----------
Combine the following into a single text file to upload:

1. Paste the updated artifacts.tsv in full.
2. Paste the updated diagnostic's registry-check section, or its
   --selftest output, showing pull-verified classification.
3. Paste the resolver test results (a-e).
4. Paste publish-image-release.sh --dry-run output, showing asset
   filenames derived from the current image list.
5. Paste MANUAL-FETCH.md Section C in full, without approval
   language.
6. Report bash syntax, ShellCheck, pre-commit, and all grep-audit
   results.
7. State explicitly: image archives remain filesystem-only and
   optional; the diagnostic default now performs real pulls to
   distinguish true failures from probe false positives;
   organisational approval is assumed in place; the learner VM was
   not accessed.
8. Leave changes uncommitted and unstaged.
